description: Committee recommends transferring $766,300 to Special Events Reserve.
This aims to stabilize funding and limit 2026-2027 event applications.
Administration will report on long-term funding by 2028.

chips.text: Local swim clubs and other event organizers will need to adapt to new intake timelines.
Mayor Block questioned if the proposed single intake would hinder quick decisions for some events.
Discover Saskatoon advocated for a strategic, differentiated approach to event funding.
The proposed "equitable distribution" of funds aims to ensure smaller events receive support.
Committee requested a report comparing Saskatoon's event funding to other municipalities.

description: Approved 2026 cash grants for environmental community groups.
Committee recommends approving servicing agreement for North Marquis GP Ltd.
Agreement enables new industrial development in Marquis Industrial Area.
Development is for Parcel C, NW   Section 21.
Committee recommends developing a city land policy for affordable housing.
Policy would guide land disposition and acquisition processes.
Policy would ensure long-term affordability for projects.

chips.text: Chair emphasized importance of long-term affordability in the new policy.
New policy replaces current ad hoc approach to city land for housing.
No conclusive research guides long-term affordable housing expiry dates.
Métis Nation–Saskatchewan strongly supports the proposed land policy.
Policy would prioritize land sales to Indigenous-led developers.
Administration will develop the policy and bring it back for approval.

description: Committee recommends RFP for River Landing Farmer's Market Building.
RFP may include 120 Sonnenschein Way as optional component.

chips.text: Committee added criteria to prioritize market success and business incubation.
Current vendors at Gather Local Market and tenants at 120 Sonnenschein Way.
Committee refined administration's RFP to include specific community benefits.
Are comparable business incubation spaces available elsewhere in Saskatoon?
Tenants want to maintain community and incubation services in the building.

description: Committee recommends new five-year license for Prairie River Cruises.
Allows river tour operations until March 31, 2031.
Includes option for additional five-year renewal.

chips.text: Mayor Block questioned why this specific license agreement required committee approval.

description: Recommends consolidating Skate Saskatoon's ACT Arena and Hall agreements.
Proposes a new five-year agreement with three renewal options.
Supports Skate Saskatoon's year-round skating programs.

chips.text: Skate Saskatoon has operated the ACT Figure Skating Arena for over 40 years.

description: Committee recommends clarifying Marr Residence board meeting support.

chips.text: Marr Residence board requested the terms of reference update.

description: Directs asset assessment and usage report for George Ward Pool.
Report findings due to Council by Q4 2026.

chips.text: Councillor glad to see motion after constituent concerns about pool closure.
Constituents opposed George Ward Pool closure and wanted options for maintenance.

description: City Council accepted the 2026 Municipal Heritage Advisory Committee Work Plan.
Public Art Advisory Committee's 2026 work plan presented to Council.
